maria: Heads-up — ran a dry-run combining prompt/prefix cache + per-entry encryption across two regions. Quick summary below, results are surprising :eyes:

chao: What was the exact test harness + runtime binary? Any kernel-selector changes?

maria: Test harness: mirror of prod traffic (sampling 0.5%), runtime-v2.1.4 (jit-quant path). Kernel selector unchanged, but I toggled AES-GCM encryption on KV store and ran two keying modes. Config snippet:

```
CACHE_KEY = HMAC_SHA256(kms_key, tenant_id || ':' || prefix_hash)
BLOOM_FILTER = 2^18 entries, 6 hash functions
ENCRYPT = AES-GCM (per-entry nonce from KMS)
KERNEL = runtime-v2.1.4 (jit-quant)
BATCHING = adaptive, target_ms=6
```

sanjay: Did you shard the bloom by tenant or keep it global? False positives would explain cross-tenant hit noise. :thinking_face:

maria: Baseline was global bloom (memory win). Runs:
- baseline (no encrypt, global bloom): cache hit 18.5%, p95 latency baseline
- encrypt + global bloom: hit 19.1%, observed cross-tenant collisions ~0.7% of hits, p95 +38ms
- encrypt + per-tenant salt + bloom shards: hit 18.9%, collisions ~0.02%, p95 +41ms (encryption overhead dominates)

Attached sample log lines:
```
[2026-05-21 14:12:33] cache_lookup tenant=acme key=HMAC(...)=0x3a2f hit=true decrypt_ms=6.8 kernel_select_ms=0.9
[2026-05-21 14:12:34] cache_miss tenant=umbrella warmup_enqueue size=128 batch_ms=5.3
```

kevin: So per-tenant salt fixes collisions but doesn't help p95 because decrypt is the bottleneck. Did you measure decrypt concurrency? Could be kernel selector thread gets scheduled differently under crypto.

maria: Yes — we observed a CPU spike pinned to the kernel-selector and decryption worker threads during warmup. Warmup (bulk prefetch) increases decrypt ops and temporarily amplifies tail. Also warmup causes KV warm paths to hold GCs longer because decrypted buffers allocated.

ellie: Can you paste the exact key derivation and truncation? Small truncation could amplify collisions.

maria: We used truncated HMAC digest for key length reasons (legacy compact keys). Example: `KEY_ID = hex(HMAC)[0:16]` — truncation + global bloom explains some overlap. Switching to full HMAC or longer slice + per-tenant salt reduced FP rate dramatically.

audit-bot: AUDIT: automated collision scan found 12 keys reused across 4 distinct tenant IDs in last 7 days (region-us-west). Creating ticket INF-842 for immediate review. Recommendation: per-tenant namespace salt + KMS-backed HMAC; rotate keys annually. :lock:

chao: For rollout I'd prefer a two-arm canary: (A) per-tenant bloom shards (no encryption) and (B) encryption+salt with hot-unencrypted cache for top-N keys. Run both on 10% traffic and compare hit-rate, p95, and CPU. Also add kernel-selector tracing to capture selector+decrypt overlap.

sanjay: I'll add a lightweight profiling hook: emit per-request phases — lookup_ms, decrypt_ms, kernel_select_ms, batch_wait_ms — and a reason tag (warmup|live). That should help attribute tail.

kevin: And consider a hybrid: keep encrypted entries on disk but maintain small tenant-scoped decrypted hot cache in RAM for top prefixes with strict eviction + audit log. That minimizes repeated decrypts. Need threat-model review though.

ellie: I'll own the dashboarding. New charts: cross-tenant collision rate, decrypt_ms p50/p95/p99, kernel_select_ms breakdown, warmup CPU delta. Set alert at collision > 0.1% or decrypt p95 > 20ms.

maria: Filing short experiment plan as INF-848: "prompt-cache encryption dry-run + perf plan" — includes configs, raw logs, and suggested canary steps. Will attach the kernel selector flame traces.

chao: Perfect. One more ask: when you run the canary, capture per-tenant memory usage for bloom shards vs global bloom to quantify memory tradeoffs.

maria: Will do. Planning canary next Wed. Thanks all :thumbsup:
